subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: What aspects of their experience are Yelp reviewers talking about?

judge.implied_focus: The dimensions of the customer restaurant experience that Yelp reviewers discuss (food, service, staff, ambiance) and their resulting recommendation stance

per_column.name: food_quality_rating
per_column.rationale: Captures the food facet of the dining experience, a core aspect reviewers discuss.

per_column.name: service_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Captures specific service-related problems, a distinct experiential facet.

per_column.name: staff_attitude
per_column.rationale: Captures the interpersonal/staff facet, complementary to service issues.

per_column.name: ambiance_atmosphere_mention
per_column.rationale: Captures the environmental/atmosphere facet of the experience.

per_column.name: overall_recommendation_stance
per_column.rationale: An outcome/summary facet reflecting the aggregate experience, naturally tied to the other aspects.

judge.rationale: All five columns cohere tightly around a single, data-inferable focus: the aspects of the restaurant experience discussed in Yelp reviews. They decompose the experience into well-separated, non-redundant facets (food, service issues, staff attitude, ambiance) plus an overall recommendation outcome, at a useful categorical granularity with meaningful value distributions and 'not_present' handling for aspect coverage. This is a sound aspect-based decomposition rather than a scattered grab-bag or generic mechanical features (no token counts or bare sentiment). The implied focus is highly actionable: an analyst can quantify which aspects dominate, correlate aspect ratings with recommendation stance, and target operational improvements. Minor deduction on structure because staff_attitude and service_issue_type partially overlap conceptually, and recommendation_stance is more an outcome than an 'aspect', slightly mixing facet types.
